newsitem.title: USA: Tampa, Fla., land swap clears way for refinancing.
newsitem.headline: Tampa, Fla., land swap clears way for refinancing.

text.p: Tampa Port Authority agreed to give City of Tampa the land on which the Florida Aquarium was built, clearing the way for the city to refinance the aquarium bonds, city officials said Tuesday.
At a meeting Monday, Port Authority also agreed to pay the aquarium up to $1.67 million over 10 years.
If Tampa city council approves the land transfer agreement at its meeting Thursday, the port would be released from its pledge to pay $10 million of aquarium debt.
The struggling aquarium was built on port land with $84 million of revenue bonds issued by the city. The bonds were backed in part $10 million letter of credit from the port.

Aquarium attendance has fallen 50 percent below projections and the facility was forced to dip into reserves to make its $3.2 million debt service payment in May. The aquarium lost $4 million in 1995, and $2.3 million in the quarter ended July 31.

The city proposed taking over the land and refinancing the bonds, which would save up to $800,000 annually on debt service. But it agreed to release the port from its letter of credit only if the land's appraised value was at least $10 million.

Appraisals on the 7.83-acre parcel ranged from $7.4 million to $17 million and the city and the port agreed to set the value at $8.33 million. The port authority agreed to make up the difference by pledging to cover $166,912 a year in revenue shortfalls for 10 years.
If the bond deal is approved, Merrill Lynch Inc would be senior manager.
